utterances.text: Were you aware that the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade also had automatic weapons with scopes, semi-automatic weapons with scopes, passive infrared sights, and other forms of optical equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we call up, please, P5930.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The document in front of you, Mr. Skrba, is dated the 29th of October, 1993. It's from the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command. The brigade is informing the command that it's in possession of rifles with optical sights, semi-automatic rifles with optical sights, machine-guns with optical sights, sniper rifles, rifles with passive infrared sights, sniper rifle silencers. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You see in the sentence below Colonel Stojanovic who signed this says: "As we don't have a special sniper unit, we have issued the sniper rifles to combatants in the subordinated units. "They are active when the combatants are in position." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You also see the next sentence where commander Colonel Stojanovic says: "In order to be more effective covering enemy territory with snipers, in front of our forward lines, we require another seven M69, 7.9-millimetre sniper rifles ..." and he asks for a further three sniper rifles with infrared sights and silencers. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This suggests, does it not, that the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade had sniper rifles, it had automatic weapons and semi-automatic weapons with scopes, it had other optical equipment, it distributed that equipment to its subordinate units, and those units used that equipment on their forward lines, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I did not receive anything myself and I did not have these weapons that are mentioned in this list ever in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you accept the thrust of this document is as I summarised it, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No, I didn't understand exactly what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'll move on after this, but is it your position still that the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade did not have sniper rifles, did not have automatic weapons with scopes, did not have semi-automatic weapons with scopes, did not have other optical equipment which can be used to shoot people accurately from a large long distance?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to object --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to say that I can't say anything about the brigade. I was not in authority in the brigade. I can talk about my company. If you know what a company is as opposed to a battalion and a brigade, you will know that I can be responsible only for the company that I was in command of. I can't say anything about the brigade. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll move now to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Karadzic, that resolved your --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yeah, it's resolved, but I would just direct your attention to the translation; namely, it should be translated: "In order to be more effective covering enemy's area in front of our lines," not "enemy's territory," but just space to the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a look. I think we can move on now. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba, we're moving now to Baba Stijena which is discussed at paragraph 11 of your statement. Towards the end of your paragraph there you describe an elderly Muslim man who herded goats at a distance of 80 to a hundred metres from Baba Stijena. I think we can agree that Baba Stijena itself affords an excellent view over that part of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar, please, to call up 2 -- 65 ter 23861, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, Mr. Skrba, do you recognise that location?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's Baba Stijena, isn't it? That's an SRK position at Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You can see from the photograph, I think, that it's quite a fortified position, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not what it looked like in 1992 and 1993 when I was a company commander. It looked rather different. It was not as fortified as you can see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was it, nevertheless, fortified in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it had to be fortified because there was constant sniper and mortar fire. That part of the road was constantly under fire. It was under the control of the BH army. The visibility in this particular part was very good. It was quite exposed and there were a lot of incidents happening over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you say that this part of the road, Baba Stijena itself, was under the control of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No, no, they controlled the road from their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Baba Stijena was always under SRK control, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that photograph, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P5938, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, while we're on Baba Stijena you said that BiH -- there was constant sniper and mortar fire on that position. Did SRK forces at Baba Stijena return mortar fire from Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No, they did not have mortars. How could they respond? And you saw the road in the photo. That was the main road leading from the eastern part of Sarajevo towards Pale, and it was exposed in that part. That's why we had to erect protective fences because people, especially civilians, were often wounded or killed in that part between Baba Stijena and Kuce, the length of that part of the road was about 100 to 150 metres. The rest of the road was not exposed because it was hidden by the woods, by the thick woods, that's where the defence line was. This part here was rather exposed all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, a note to clarify your evidence: Are you suggesting that if SRK forces at Baba Stijena came under sniper fire from the ABiH side, that they would not return fire; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I'm saying when a car came by, either civilian or a military vehicle, it was always exposed to either sniper or mortar or rifle fire. There was a time --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: -- when no car could drive by without being attacked --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'm going to have to ask you to concentrate very carefully on my questions. Is it your position that if SRK forces at Baba Stijena came under sniper fire from the ABiH side that they would not return fire?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: When people's lives were threatened, only on those occasions, that's when fire was returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, I want to turn to paragraph 6 of your statement. You refer to units of a brigade of the ABiH and you say at the end of paragraph 6 that: "These Muslim units also had their positions in-depth exclusively in civilian facilities and houses." You see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: How did you gather that information?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: We saw it ourselves. Those positions were so close that they could be observed from our locations - our positions were better in tactical terms than theirs - and we either heard or saw it ourselves. There was no military facility anywhere near. We all lived there. We were familiar with all the wells, houses, the river. When I was a kid I used to take that same road with my father to go to Sarajevo. I went to school every day taking that road. So we were familiar with all of the houses and all of the features in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you return fire to those units if they fired at you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: We returned in most cases. Whenever they attacked or tried a breakthrough, whenever they were redeployed in order to conquer one part of our territory, we held one part of road and our task was to defend that road and the villages in-depth behind our lines. That was our objective, an objective we achieved. It should be known those villages were ethnically Serbian, purely Serbian villages. There were no other ethnicities living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Who authorised you to fire at ABiH positions located in civilian facilities and houses?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: We did not shoot at civilian houses. We opened fire on their lines which were in our immediate vicinity whenever we were provoked, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in your own statement you say that the Muslim units had their positions in-depth exclusively in civilian facilities and houses. That's at paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: And that's true. In-depth 100 or 200 metres, that's the forward line. And the civilian facilities, the civilian houses, were the positions of their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, what measures did you take to minimise civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Well, we opened fire only when we observed a target. We fired at specific targets, only ... and we fired when needed, we did not use unnecessary fire ... so that the combat units we had were used as little as possible, our infantry. This meant that if a platoon came under attack then that platoon would open fire while the other unit, company, was deployed in such a way that they did not fire at all. This meant that our platoons or squads fired in response to attacks from their forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the interpreter didn't get the end of your answer. Could you repeat the end of your last answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: If we came under attack by the BH army, we retaliated, we returned fire, in the place where we were provoked and attacked. On no occasion was the entire company engaged in the defence, only certain squads or platoons were. We never opened random fire as there was no need for that. Besides, bullets were expensive and in short supply.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, it's your evidence that your company was essentially a small arms company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that bullets were expensive and they were in short supply. Can this be recorded because it was not recorded the first time around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. CLSS will check it later on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And also that the platoons that had come under attack would defend themselves, that the defence was not carried out by the entire company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Skrba, could you speak slow -- a bit slower so that the interpreters can follow your answers. Yes, Mr. Gaynor, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is it correct that your --

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: -- your company was using rifles, automatic weapons, semi-automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: When using those weapons, what steps did you as company commander take to ensure that your troops could distinguish between civilians and combatants?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I made sure that fire was opened scarcely on an observed target. We always emphasized that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: How did your troops know what they were firing at?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: They saw them. Our lines were not far from theirs, and one could observe with the naked eye what trench was fired from, what bunker was fired from. It was easy to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And as well as that you, no doubt, had optical equipment, such as binoculars, specialised scopes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No, we did not have those because we did not need them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your evidence is that your entire company did not have any optical equipment, no binoculars, no scopes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: That's my evidence. We didn't need them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And your company was, in fact, specialised small arms company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: It was not a specialised company. It was just a regular small arms company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I ask the Registrar for map 1D8529, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said small arms or infantry company. The interpreter chose to use the word "small arms" instead of "infantry." That's on line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll move on now. Now, Mr. Registrar, if you could, in fact, focus in on the red box, please, and indeed that's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Skrba, on this map you've marked an 82-millimetre mortar position and you said: "That was the only place on that road where there was a mortar position." That's at paragraph 10. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I think if we look closely at this map we can see the yellow road at the top which is the Pale road and then a little bit south of your circle -- your red circle we see a white road which appears to be a more minor road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, your red circle does not appear to be actually on a road marked on this map. So could you clarify whether this red circle referred --

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Well, that is close to the Velesici road where you go up and down. That's that part a bit enlarged, so it seems that it is not close but it is close to that white road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So was the 82-millimetre mortar located on a road or on a dirt track or in a field? Where was it located?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I don't know because it was not in my zone of responsibility, but I know that next to the road that it was there because I saw it as I travelled along the road. I don't know whose piece that was. It was not in my area of responsibility. That mortar was not in my area of responsibility. That zone, that area, belonged to a different unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, how much longer would you need? I'm asking for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm willing to break at any stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then we passed the time to break so we'll break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then shall we resume at half past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.41 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I'll just take this opportunity to note for the record that the still photo of Baba Stijena identified by the witness and admitted as P5938 is a still from a film made by a BBC TV crew which appeared in the BBC Panorama programme, and that episode of Panorama was made by Martin Bell and it's referred to at paragraph 59 of P1996 which is the amalgamated statement of Martin Bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Skrba, I'll continue my questions now. We were looking at the picture which is on the screen in front of you, and I just want to take you up on the point where you said that you saw the 82-millimetre position as you travelled along the road. Now, are you referring to the white road to the east of your red circle?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: This road, this earth road that you see going to the east --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I assist for the accuracy of the transcript. The general said Martin Bell recorded this in 1996 and it's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The P1996 is the amalgamated statement of Martin Bell. I didn't mention the year 1996 as far as I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, perhaps at this stage I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the court usher to help you with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And I would like you to identify the earth road - along which you travelled - with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Fine. So the roads that you've marked on this map were under SRK control in 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In fact, they were under SRK control for the duration of the conflict; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, roads in our territory where you could move freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And what kinds of vehicles could you move freely along those roads in?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Passenger vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Presumably with specialised military trucks you could drive along those roads that you've marked as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: It was difficult because these are narrow roads from the Austro-Hungarian times and the curves are pretty big. You can see that for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I accept that. Now, if you were to drive a jeep along these roads rather than a very large military vehicle, it wouldn't pose any particular difficulty, would it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: A jeep, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask you to sign and date that map, please, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P5939, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Staying with that map, under whose control was the 82-millimetre mortar position that you opened?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I don't know. Not -- not with my companies. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In your statement at paragraph 10 you say: "That is the" -- you're referring here to the red dot marking 82-millimetre position. You say: "That is the only place on that road where there was a mortar position. I claim that at that or other positions in the vicinity there were no 120-millimetre-calibre mortars." What period of time are you referring to with that statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: The period 1992 to 1993 and then periodically until the end of the war. I was the company commander, an active company commander, in that company. So it would be the period 1992/1993, the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So you accept that there may have been 120-millimetre mortars in that general area in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Well, I cannot agree if I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'd like to bring up now a map where you describe the area of responsibility of your company, 1D08530, please. We see the red line along the Pale road which marks the front edge of your zone of responsibility; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you be able to take a pen and mark the area of Palez on this map?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I don't know where Palez is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you were the --

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: -- you were the company commander, this was your zone of responsibility, and you are claiming that you don't know where the Palez area is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Perhaps it had a different name, but I don't really see here where that is. If there is no marking of some sort, then I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, let me clarify. The area of Palez is not marked on this particular map. We're going to see it in a minute on a different map. But I'm asking you if you are claiming that you don't know or are not able to identify where the area of Palez is on this map. Is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Perhaps I do know it but under a different name, but like this on this map I don't see that place I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Under what other name do you know the area Palez?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know until you show me which part it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the registrar, please, to call up 65 ter 23919E, please. Could we turn this by 90 degrees, please, and zoom in on the centre part of this map, please. And if you could go a little further to the south, please, and zoom in, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you see the word "Palez" there, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, it's clear when we compare the previous map to this map that Palez is exactly within your zone of responsibility. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, we'll come back to that map a little later, but for the moment did you know that the SRK had 120-millimetre mortars in the Palez area during the year 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we call up, please, 65 ter 23880.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where do we see Palez on this map -- it has gone already.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we will be coming back to it later but I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's gone. If you come back later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we go to the second page in B/C/S, third page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is a document as I think you can see, Mr. Witness, from the SRK command dated the 9th of May, 1995, the header refers to "Talas 2," which can be translated in English as Wave 2. Now if we look at paragraph 3, this is at the bottom of page 3 in English and at the middle of page 2 in the original, we see a reference at the end of that paragraph to SRK objectives, including to: "Place a major part of Stari Grad under fire control with the objective of ultimate victory." If we turn to the next page in English staying on the same page in the original, paragraph 4 begins with the words: "I have decided ..." And then towards the end of the paragraph he refers to: " ... for ultimately crushing the enemy's defensive power and for placing a major part of Stari Grad under fire control ..." Do you see that, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You know where Stari Grad is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stari Grad includes areas such as Bascarsija and the Markale Market, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, can we see in the Serbian where that is -- ah, this is paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 at the end is a reference to Stari Grad and at paragraph 4 there's a further reference to placing a major part of Stari Grad under fire control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if we turn now to the next page in English and the next page in the original and we look at the end of paragraph 5.1. I think we need to go back a page in B/C/S. The last sentence he says: "Everything shall be planned out by the deputy chief of artillery Major Savo Simic." Mr. Witness, you know Savo Simic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether the witness said "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, do you know Savo Simic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. We'll carry on. At the bottom of page 6 in English, paragraph 6 reads: "Forces carrying out combat operations in the Debelo Brdo area are supported by an 82-millimetre MB and a 120-millimetre battery from the sector of Trebevic-Palez." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: MB means mortar platoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No. MB means "minobacac," mortar, 82-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now if we can turn to page 7 in English and page 5 in B/C/S, paragraph 7.1(a), this refers to ammunition for the tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In the middle of the paragraph it says that the 1st Smbr and the DIO units will be approved for the following for the execution of the offensive operations in the Debelo Brdo area, and it lists, among others, 100 shells for the 120-millimetre mortar platoon. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So do you accept that according to this document the SRK had 120-millimetre mortars in the Palez area?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the last page so that we can identify the whole document, whether it's complete and whether it's signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps we can ask the witness to answer the question first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, could you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Well, I cannot entirely answer the question because I don't know. I really didn't see and I did not take part in these kinds of events because my infantry company's responsibility did not lie in Debelo Brdo. We were behind in control under a certain angle. I don't know whether these are preparatory actions for an operation. I don't know whether this happened or not. I mean, this is something that would need to be done at the corps level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, do you accept that Palez did fall within your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Until 1993, though, because later I'm not sure about it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, you haven't mentioned anything about that in your statement, have you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I cannot say that there was a mortar there because I don't know. I did not manage to find out in any way if there was a mortar or not in this place called Palez.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender the document that we've just been discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, could we please see what this document is; and secondly, the witness did not confirm anything from this document, so I was not allowed to tender documents under the same circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, this document is directly relevant to the witness's assertion as to whether the SRK had 120-millimetre mortars in the Palez area in 1995. He did discuss the document to some extent. It goes directly to his credibility and it goes directly to the matters -- the claims he makes in his statement. I believe that it does form an integral part of his evidence so far and it is vital for assessing his credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do you challenge the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I'm not sure. I haven't seen all of it. I'm not sure about the signature. And also, I'm not sure whether the operation was carried out or whether it was just being planned and whether he was there at all. All in all, all of this is rather dubious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow you saying so. You can see the document on your own with your e-court. You have all the legal associates in the courtroom who can see the document. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, you have more options with e-court than I do. I cannot actually look at it myself. It would -- the page would have to be shown to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you explain the format of the document, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A document is attached to the previous -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: As far as we could tell, the front page which is a 5th of May SRK command document, 5th of May, 1995, is not related to this document. The two are under this -- this 65 ter number, but I don't believe the two documents are related. And in respect of its authenticity, I note that it does not appear to be signed; however, it appears to certainly be prepared with exactly the same type face as many of the SRK documents that we've already seen and have been admitted in evidence. I don't believe there's ever been a single SRK document so far in the trial where authenticity has been a question. And I can certainly provide more information to the Court as to where this document was seized from if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not hear everything, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just wanted to respond to one assertion and get some clarification from Mr. Robinson. Mr. Karadzic suggested that he was not permitted to have such documents introduced during the course of his case. I wanted to confirm that when matters of credibility and impeachment arose and was stated as such by Mr. Robinson, that I would repeatedly rise and affirm that, indeed, that was another basis for admission. And I believe the Defence will confirm that approach during the course of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's true that during the Prosecution case for the most part when we had a document that contradicted the testimony -- purported to contradict the testimony of the witness, it was admitted when -- even if the witness couldn't confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber agrees with Mr. Gaynor and this will be admitted as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P5940, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Mr. President. Could we now call up 65 ter 23926, please. If we could go to the next page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We see there a signature of Savo Simic, who is -- has the same name as a Savo Simic referred to in the previous document. You see that, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now in this document we see if we go to the previous page in B/C/S and the same page in English, under item 1(b) it says: "Fire support for the 3/1st Smbr and SRK DIO carrying out b/d at Debelo Brdo and Vranjaca shall be realised using: "120-millimetre mortar battery (4 artillery pieces) from the Palez area." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And do you accept that b/d -- or tell us what "b/d" stands for.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I'm not an artillery man, so I don't know what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in B/C/S, please, and onto the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Under item 5 it says: "Readiness for action on the 15th of May, 1995, at 0500 hours." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you accept, Mr. Skrba, that on the basis of this document signed by Major Savo Simic, it appears that there were 120-millimetre mortar positions, four of them, at the Palez area at the time that this document was drafted. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could explain to the Chamber why you don't?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: The reason is simple. It is because in my opinion there were no mortars at the time at Palez. As for them being prepared for some sort of action, that's a different matter. But as I saw those 82-millimetre mortars in the vicinity, well, they should have been 120-millimetre mortars. I don't know whether they brought them in. I don't believe that was the case, though. So in my opinion those 120-millimetre mortars were not set up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So you -- it's your position, is it, that the assertion that there were four 120-millimetre mortars in Palez at the time that this document was drafted is incorrect; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document for the same reasons as previously advanced, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, next Exhibit P5941.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to paragraph 15 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Line 7 the witness didn't say they should have been, he said that 120-millimetre mortars were not there. So this is just a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I will move on now. At paragraph 15 of your statement, Mr. Skrba, you say: "Between Petrovici village and the Sarajevo city there were no artillery weapons or mortars." Could you clarify what period of time you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: To the period running from the beginning of the war until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you accept that the Palez area is, roughly speaking, approximately between Petrovici village and the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No, it's a little to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, we'll look at a map now so we can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: First of all, could I call up D718.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The map we're about to see, Mr. Skrba, is a VRS map showing confrontation lines and VRS assets around the city of Sarajevo. Mr. Skrba, south of the city of Sarajevo do you see the Cyrillic letters 1.Smbr?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you tell us what that abbreviation stands for?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I'm not sure but perhaps the 1st Sarajevo Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Fair enough. And while we're on this point, is that brigade sometimes referred to as the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I couldn't say for certain. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you see an area marked by dotted red lines around the area where the 1st Smbr marking is? Essentially what I'm asking you is: Do you see the area of responsibility of the 1st Sarajevo Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps just for the sake of clarity if I could ask the usher to assist you with a pen. If you could just fairly quickly draw around the area of responsibility of the 1st Sarajevo Motorised Brigade and then sign and date this map, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I can't mark this because I wasn't in the brigade. I was a company member. I mentioned what the responsibilities of my company were, but I can't agree with this map because I didn't deal with such matters and I can't be familiar with what the responsibilities were of the 1st Sarajevo Motorised Brigade, and that is why I cannot make any markings on this map and draw the lines designating the areas of responsibility of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right, well I'll leave it to Their Honours to decide. We'll look at a more blown-up version. It certainly appears to any reasonable observer that the red dots appear to be intended to indicate the zone of responsibility of the 1st Smbr.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I call up, please, 65 ter 23919E. This is a blown-up portion of the map we've just been looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think you know, Mr. President, what I'm going to say, but we would appreciate Mr. Gaynor refraining from comments about what's perfectly obvious, and I think it's perfectly obvious he knows better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Robinson. As soon as the map I've just referred to comes in, we'll have a look at the location of the village of Petrovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was able to see Petrovici if we zoom in on this map as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We could use it. The next one is a higher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: -- definition version. Now, if we could rotate that by 90 degrees, please, and essentially focus on the bottom 50 per cent of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, there we see at the bottom of the map part of the Cyrillic letters 1.Smbr, don't we, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And above the letter M we see the word "Petrovici," don't we?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In fact, if we could focus on the word "Petrovici," Mr. Registrar, I think it's fair to say, Mr. Witness, that we can see a number of black dots which appear to indicate buildings making up the village of Petrovici; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now I'm going to put it to you that that's quite a considerable distance from the first map we saw at the start of your testimony, which you claimed was a line on the edge of the village of Petrovici; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Miljevici, Kozarevici, and Petrovici are ethnically pure villages --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's last word.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you finish your answer, please, Mr. Witness. The interpreter missed the last part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I didn't just say that we stopped only in front of the village of Petrovici, we stopped at the edge of the village. The first village from Sarajevo is Miljevici and then you have Kozarevici and then Petrovici, so we were at the edge of villages that are ethnically pure. If it's any clearer to you I'll tell you what the distance is in kilometres between Petrovici and the lines where we were up to the road for Trebevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You were trying to keep those villages ethnically pure; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this permissible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were trying to mount a defence of those villages. We didn't want to maintain them as ethnically pure villages because they were already ethnically pure Serbian villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: All right. Let's just look back at the map again. If you move north from Petrovici towards the city of Sarajevo, do you see a large shaded area west of Studenkovici, and in the middle of that large shaded area do you see the Cyrillic letters B-r-A-G?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The abbreviation BrAG stands for brigade artillery groups, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You see the word "Palez" at the top of the shaded area of the brigade artillery groups, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And the 82-millimetre mortar that you identified earlier was located approximately where? Perhaps we can ask the usher to ask you to mark the map.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you put 82-millimetre next to that, sign and date this, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So looking at this map, Mr. Witness, and taking into account the documents that we've seen, it's fair to say, isn't it, that in the general area between Petrovici and Sarajevo city the SRK had a considerable presence of mortar and artillery assets, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please be assisted. Could we be told when the map was made, who made it, and does it reflect the actual situation at the time or the situation as it was supposed to be in the future, the situation for which plans had been made. We can't draw any conclusions on this basis. If a certain action has been planned and then markings made to indicate the location of weapons, it doesn't mean that this is actually going to happen. So we have to know what this map actually represents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, first of all, the witness's position is that throughout the conflict there were no artillery or mortar assets between Petrovici and the city of Sarajevo. That's his position. Second, this is certainly something that the accused can take up in re-examination if he wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. Mr. Skrba, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the ground between Petrovici up until Miljevici, as far as Miljevici is very steep, it's a mountainous area, it's very difficult terrain. The villages here, Petrovici, for example, and Tilava are separated by a hill at Palez that the gentleman has mentioned. It's on a hill, it's on the slopes of Trebevica. This part from Petrovici to Sarajevo, the areas we moved through, in fact, is a road in Petrovici, Kozarevici, Stanovici, Miljevici, there were no artillery weapons nor in the area of responsibility of my company. As for the other areas, I don't know. This is a very detailed map and I would be grateful if you could not continue putting questions to me about the artillery resources because I'm not an artillery man. If you have any questions about infantry weapons, I'll answer those questions. But you will have other witnesses who will be in a position to answer your questions about the artillery and mortars. There is really nothing that I could tell you with any certainty about such matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, first of all I'd like to tender the map marked by the witness. He seems to have put some extra markings on it, but I don't think they affect the location of the 82-millimetre mortar position he marked earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he put the date of this on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you put the date --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: -- it's the 22nd of October, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could this be the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P5942, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrba my final question is that on the basis of your answers, do you accept that the SRK may have had 120-millimetre mortar positions in the area south of Sarajevo in August 1995 that you might not have been aware of?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Just one clarification, please. When you say to the "south of Sarajevo," what area are you referring to? Perhaps you could show me on a map and then I could answer that question with greater accuracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You can answer it with whatever modifications you wish. If you like, do you accept that there were areas within the area of operation of the 1st Smbr in August 1995 which might have contained 120-millimetre mortar positions that you were unaware of?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I wouldn't want to comment. I wouldn't want to answer that question because I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So you accept the possibility that you were not aware of all of the 120-millimetre mortar positions of the SRK in the area of responsibility of the 1st Smbr in August 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I wasn't familiar with matters that concern the artillery or with mortars, so I don't know where they were positioned or who manned them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I wanted to follow-up on one point concerning P5940 which is a document Mr. Karadzic raised a concern that he did not see a stamp or a signature at the end of the document. Mr. Reid has kindly looked into the matter and we do have the final page, which for some reason was not in e-court, which bears the ERN 05292954. It contains the signature and stamp of Major-General Dragomir Milosevic, and I'm happy to provide a hard copy of the final page to Your Honours and to the Defence right now. And we will have the final page translated and uploaded to e-court as soon as we can. And we understand that the final page will form part of P5940.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to eliminate the first page of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do that as well, Your Honour. Good point. We'll take away the first document as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done. Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions. I think we will be done very quickly, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Skrba, in paragraph 10 of your statement you stated that you had relatives who resided in Studenkovici and that you often visited them and that you did not see mortar positions in the vicinity of Studenkovici village, i.e., on that axis. I'm talking about 120-millimetre mortars. Does this also refer to August 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up P5940.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May it be noted that there is a lot of background noise in the courtroom and it's very hard to hear either the accused or the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document you were talking about preparatory orders. When it comes to preparatory orders, is every one of them implemented?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page, please. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under 5 does it say the Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade will continue offensive activities on the ring facing Treskavica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page where it says "combat-readiness." I apologise, it says combat-readiness for the attack on the 15th of May. This is the last sentence in the first paragraph on the very top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the paragraph that refers to Debelo Brdo which is perhaps either at the bottom of this page or on the following page. The following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this document speak about something that happened or is it also a preparatory order for some upcoming actions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: In my view -- I'm not sure. However, in my view this is an order for preparations, for some sort of preparations, I don't know of what kind, whether it's preparations for defence or for something else. I don't know what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When it comes to the planning of such operations where additional units are planned, are additional assets also planned, those that do not normally exist in the area; however, if this operation is carried out they will be necessary?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: As far as I know, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what is Debelo Brdo? Is that a civilian settlement or is it just a bare mountaintop or a slope on Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: As the name speaks for itself, Golo Brdo is a bare hill slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are no civilian settlements there, are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Almost none, perhaps a few houses along the edge of the hilltop and that's where the positions of the units were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection. I've only risen now, but I wish to remind Mr. Karadzic to refrain from making leading questions. He can't pretend he doesn't know the rule by now. He must refrain from leading questions in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Are you done, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did we occupy Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS SKRBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for the witness, Your Excellencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Skrba, that concludes your evidence and on behalf of the Tribunal I'd like to thank you to testify in this case, and now you are free to go. Please have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will adjourn for the day, not deducting the time from the Defence case. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. There are a couple of things, yes. Excuse me. Mr. Robinson, the Chamber has received two filings, a revised notification with respect to two witnesses whose request for protective measures have been denied. What's the point of maintaining the pseudonyms in the filings? Probably you need to re-file them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I did that because it was unclear until this morning whether those witnesses would have the opportunity to address the Court, but now that you've made it clear we can file it publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. There's one further matter which is today the accused filed a request for leave to reply a motion for videolink and consideration of protective measures for Witness KW-533. Given the limited scope of the proposed reply, the Chamber will grant the request pursuant to Rule 126 bis of the Rules and orders that the accused file his reply no later than Tuesday, 23rd of October, 2012. One more thing, shall we go into private session, but before that we can excuse the -- the witness can be excused. Thank you, Mr. Skrba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we in private session? Yes, shall we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of October, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.38 p.m.,
